summary: Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Boston University in 2001, where he studied under Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries, as well as Trashichöling. He held professorships at Minzu University of China and Tibet University, and directed the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He served as professor at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College, and Sanskrit College and University, also holding a post at Calcutta.

Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri and also studied under R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.

Dwarikadas Shastri (born 1922) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He founded Bauddha Bharati and served as an associate editor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was an Indologist and historian. He pursued his education at Presidency University from approximately 1957 to 1959, Patna University from 1959 to 1961, and the University of Calcutta between circa 1961 and 1964.

Dwijendra Nath Shukla was an Indologist and historian who earned a D.Litt. from the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer. He held a position at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, attested in 1958.

Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London and completed his PhD at the Catholic University of Louvain by 2018, where he also worked as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (born 1964) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen, taught at Naropa University in 1990, and founded Mangala Shri Bhuti.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (born 1965) studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. An active Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure, he founded Nitartha Institute, Nitartha International, and Nalandabodhi, and directed the Kamalashila Institute.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse (born 1961) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS under Dilgo Khyentse, Dudjom Rinpoche, and others, and founded Siddhartha's Intent, Khyentse Foundation, and Deer Park Institute.

Dörte Kamarid is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

E. E. Evans-Pritchard (1902–1973) studied at Exeter College, Oxford, and the London School of Economics. He taught at the London School of Economics, Cairo University, Cambridge, and served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1946 to 1970.
E. Easwaran Nampoothiry (born 1930) is an Indologist who studied under S. Venkitasubramonia Iyer. He was a lecturer in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Kerala, attested in 1973.

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Washington, Leiden, and other institutions under Turrell V. Wylie and Dezhung Rinpoche. He worked at the Library of Congress and founded the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

E. J. Rapson (1861–1937) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he worked at the British Museum and served as Professor of Sanskrit at UCL and Cambridge.

E. Michael Mendelson (1928–2024) was a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He pursued his academic studies at King's College, Cambridge (circa 1946–1949), the University of Paris (circa 1950–1952), and the University of Chicago (circa 1952–1956).

E. R. Sreekrishna Sarma (1922–1994) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Marburg between circa 1951 and 1954, and later held a post at Sri Venkateswara University, attested in 1977.

E. W. Adikaram (1905–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he became the principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Eberhard Fischer (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Basel in 1965, directed Museum Rietberg from 1972 to 1998, and later led the Rietberg-Gesellschaft and SLSA.
